To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the ionization signal produced by Compton recoil electrons in liquid argon is proportional to the electron energy, • the ionization signals produced in liquid Ar−N 2 mixtures are proportional to the ionization energy of the ionizing particle, and • this proportionality holds for all particles with ionizing energy above a few keV, including electrons, alpha-particles and protons.

the use of liquid Ar–N2 mixtures in TPCs is a viable option for the detection of low energy gamma-rays, provided that the Nitrogen concentration is kept below a few percent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a TPC filled with a mixture of liquid Argon with a concentration of Nitrogen in the range 5-15%, is a very promising approach for the detection of the 10.5 MeV gamma-ray line from the resonant band in the Nitrogen absorption spectra.

the ionization produced by Compton-electrons in a liquid Ar−N 2 TPC is well described by a simple model based on the ionization produced in pure liquid Argon, while alpha-particle ionization is well described by interpolation between the ionization produced with pure Nitrogen and pure Argon.
The main takeaway from our work is that

liquid Argon−Nitrogen mixtures are suitable for the detection of protons with energies in the range 100 keV-1 MeV, which are the ones of interest for the detection of the gamma-rays in the Nitrogen resonant band.
, in the case of Nitrogen concentrations below 5%, the detection of Compton electrons and protons in a liquid Argon−Nitrogen mixture is feasible with the same detector.
, in the case of Nitrogen concentration up to 15%, the energy resolution for Compton electrons and the energy loss for alpha-particles are not significantly altered.
